questions.stem:
Antonia Olivia Dolan and colleagues had musicians and nonmusicians with clinically average hearing listen to recordings of nature sounds and music in popular genres like acoustic folk and funk and adjust the volume to optimize their listening enjoyment. The researchers found that for a given recording that a musician and nonmusician identified as their favorite among those included in the study, optimal volume tended to be higher for the musician than for the nonmusician. Thus, if a musician and nonmusician both identified Jose Gonzalez’s “Heartbeats” as their favorite recording and the musician preferred to listen to it at a volume of 82.2 decibels, the nonmusician would be expected to __________

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: find listening to “Heartbeats” at 82.2 decibels less enjoyable than listening to it at a lower volume.
options.B: prefer listening to other music at 82.2 decibels over listening to “Heartbeats” at that volume.
options.C: enjoy listening to the nature sounds at 82.2 decibels more than listening to “Heartbeats” at 82.2 decibels.
options.D: not find it enjoyable to listen to any recordings at a volume as low as 82.2 decibels.

Recent years, architects have heightened their focus on developing eco-conscious and sustainable buildings, as exemplified by TreeVilla at Forest Hills, a structure conceived by architecture BRIO. One way to accomplish this goal is through biophilic design, which seeks to augment occupants’ emotional and physical well-being by establishing a coherent relationship among the building, nature, and human biology. Along with using ecologically sensitive construction materials, biophilic designs incorporate organic or biomorphic forms and textures. Curves, therefore, are common design features because they ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: are common in building designs in many different regions and cultures.
options.B: prioritize practicality over the personal aesthetic preferences of the architect.
options.C: are reminiscent of the arcing and contours found among plants and animals.
options.D: emphasize the aesthetic distinction between nature and architecture.

questions.stem:
Pointing to Scandinavian countries, where citizens report high levels of confidence in one another, some political scientists hold that widespread social trust enables governments to build effective, impartial institutions. Citing cases in which reforms to courts and civil services were followed by rising public confidence, other scholars hold the inverse: that trust is a product of institutions that treat citizens fairly. Political scientist Mireille Okonkwo has recently argued that both camps assume a one-directional causal relationship between two phenomena that in fact continually shape each other.

Based on the text, Okonkwo would most likely agree with which statement about social trust?

options.A: It cannot be adequately explained as simply either a precondition for or an outcome of effective institutions.
options.B: It is better understood as a consequence of impartial institutions than as a cause of them.
options.C: It varies more widely across countries than either group of scholars has acknowledged.
options.D: It plays a smaller role in the development of institutions than either group of scholars claims.

The following text is adapted from Guy de Maupassant's 1884 short story "A Recollection," from the collection Guy de Maupassant Short Stories (translated by Albert M.C. McMaster et al. in 1903). The narrator is taking a boat down the Seine river from Paris, France, to the surrounding countryside.

I took up a position in the bows [front of the boat], standing up and looking at the quays, the trees, the houses and the bridges disappearing behind us. And suddenly I perceived the great viaduct of Point du Jour which blocked the river. It was the end of Paris, the beginning of the country, and behind the double row of arches the Seine, suddenly spreading out as though it had regained space and liberty, became all at once the peaceful river which flows through the plains, alongside the wooded hills, amid the meadows, along the edge of the forests.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.A: The narrator is anxious for the trip to the countryside to be over as quickly as possible, and is frustrated that it is taking so long.
options.B: The narrator perceives a parallel between the shift from the urban environment to the countryside and the changes in the features of the river itself.
options.C: The narrator is surprised to see that the boat is taking him out of the city but is exhilarated by the opportunity to explore an unknown place.
options.D: The narrator contrasts his feelings of apprehension with the apparent tranquility of the river as the boat enters the countryside.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

When searching for atmospheric biosignatures on exoplanets, astrobiologists prioritize chemical disequilibria—the simultaneous presence of gases that would rapidly react and destroy each other unless continuously replenished by biological activity. For example, detecting methane $\mathrm{CH}_4$ in an oxygen-rich $\mathrm{O}_2$ atmosphere is considered strong evidence of life because photochemical reactions driven by stellar ultraviolet radiation break down methane into water and carbon dioxide within decades. However, planetary modeler Dr. Kevin Zahnle cautions that finding atmospheric methane alone, in the absence of abundant oxygen or ozone, cannot serve as a reliable biosignature because ______
Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: abiotic processes, such as serpentinization and volcanic outgassing, can sustain high methane levels on lifeless rocky worlds.
options.B: oxygen and methane cannot coexist in any planetary atmosphere regardless of biological activity.
options.C: microbial methanogens on Earth do not release methane into the atmosphere in measurable quantities.
options.D: ultraviolet radiation from stars accelerates biological photosynthesis while suppressing abiotic geologic emissions.

The following text is from Ralph Waldo Emerson’s 1841 essay “The Method of Nature.”

The scholars are the priests of that thought which establishes the foundations of the earth.

No matter what is their special work or profession, they stand for the spiritual interest of the world, and it is a common calamity if they neglect their post in a country where the material interest is so predominant as it is in America.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.A: In a country whose citizens are largely preoccupied with tangible gains, it is crucial that some people work to foster and preserve ideas.
options.B: The habit of intellectuals of privileging ideas over material things invariably leads to tragedy.
options.C: It is important for Americans of all kinds to have at least some military experience if society is to function properly.
options.D: Scholars have played an important role in society for a much longer time than have those people who are mainly concerned with financial gain.

questions.stem:
Several sociologists have observed that the word "culture," though commonly used in academic literature, is an ultimately hazy concept --- for example, Renate Mayntz has noted that "there is (still) no agreement on the meaning of this core term of sociological analysis." Does the idea of culture encompass art, or customs, or both these things and others? For casual usage, such haziness is permissible --- we know culture when we see it --- but for researchers, a standardization of the term is called for if sociology is to truly progress.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.A: Nonspecialists and specialists have different ideas of what the word "culture" means.
options.B: There is no widely agreed-upon definition of the word "culture," though the field of sociology would benefit if there were.
options.C: In her research, Mayntz presented reasons why sociologists disagree on how to analyze "culture."
options.D: Art and customs are key components of what nonspecialists refer to as "culture."

Milena Mohri and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis of 330 studies to investigate the effect of soil characteristics, including pH, on the capacity of Festuca rubra and 47 other plant species to absorb chromium and other heavy metals from soil through their roots. Given that in soil, metal solubility (a key determinant of plants’ metal uptake) negatively correlates with soil pH in the rhizosphere (soil immediately proximate to roots), the researchers hypothesized that plants’ total metal content would negatively correlate with soil pH, but instead they found no correlation between the two variables overall. To explain the finding, they noted that many of the included studies didn’t specify whether the reported soil profiles were those of the rhizosphere. Which statement, if true, would best account for Mohri and colleagues’ explanation?

options.A: Because of their distinct chemical properties, different heavy metals exhibit varying degrees of solubility response to changes in soil pH in the rhizosphere.
options.B: Relative concentrations of soluble metals in the rhizosphere are more strongly mediated by soil characteristics other than soil pH.
options.C: Biochemical interactions between plant roots and adjacent soil can considerably alter soil chemistry, including soil pH.
options.D: Plant species vary considerably in how deeply their root systems extend beyond the topsoil layer, where soil pH and metal concentrations are typically measured.
